title: Designing, Powering, and Optimizing AI Infrastructure at Scale
summary: Discover how Celestica designs, powers, and optimizes AI infrastructure at scale. Explore our integrated solutions for high-performance networking, storage, and liquid cooling.

AI workloads are driving unprecedented demands for compute performance, network bandwidth, storage throughput, power, and cooling. Meeting those demands requires more than compute alone; networking, storage, power, cooling, rack-level integration, and infrastructure services must work together as a single integrated system to move massive volumes of data reliably at scale.


Celestica brings production-available networking and storage platform solutions together with rack integration, liquid cooling deployments, modular power and data center solutions, and end-to-end lifecycle services to help hyperscalers and enterprises design, manufacture, power, and optimize AI infrastructure at scale.


Through custom design solutions and technology-partner collaborations, Celestica plays a key role in defining emerging compute architectures, focusing on the high-performance infrastructure required to power them at scale.


## Designing the Foundation for AI Compute


AI infrastructure depends on moving massive volumes of data quickly and consistently across large clusters. For distributed AI workloads, much of that traffic travels north-south through servers, accelerators, and storage systems rather than east-west traffic into and out of the data center. That makes high-bandwidth, low-latency networking essential to minimizing traffic bottlenecks and maintaining performance across the cluster.


Celestica’s networking portfolio is designed for these high-performance environments, with data center switching platforms in production supporting speeds up to an[industry-leading 1.6T](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/networking) to enable the bandwidth required by next-generation AI and machine learning infrastructure. Celestica's market leadership in this space was recently validated by[Dell'Oro Group](https://www.delloro.com/news/ai-back-end-networks-switch-sales-surpass-front-end-networks-for-the-first-time-in-2q2026/) , which named Celestica as the market leader in AI back-end Ethernet switch sales for Q1 and Q2 2026.


Storage must keep pace as well. The Helma supercomputer at Germany’s NHR@FAU[pairs ten Celestica SC6100 PCIe Gen5 storage controllers](https://www.celestica.com/uploadedFiles/Site/our-expertise/platform-solutions/case-studies/Xinnor_Case_Study.pdf) with Xinnor xiRAID and Lustre to serve 768 NVIDIA H100/H200 GPUs. The system ranks #3 overall on the current IO500 Production List and #1 among Lustre-based systems, demonstrating Celestica’s role as a hardware foundation for high-throughput, resilient AI/HPC storage architectures.


## Integrating the Rack as a Complete System


[Rack integration](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/platform-solutions/rack-integration-services) similarly becomes a critical link between system design and successful deployment for high-density AI infrastructure. A modern AI rack may combine compute, networking, storage, power distribution and increasingly sophisticated thermal-management technologies. By aligning high-performance networking and cluster-optimized storage with rack-level integration, Celestica helps customers design an infrastructure foundation for supporting AI workloads at scale.


Celestica provides integrated rack solutions spanning design, engineering, integration, configuration, validation, logistics and commissioning for applicable joint designs, custom, or platform-integration programs. By bringing these disciplines together, customers can rely on Celestica to provide end-to-end solutions, thereby reducing the complexity around the acquisition and installation of the associated high-density infrastructure while accelerating the transition from design to deployment.


This system-level approach also allows power, cooling and connectivity requirements to be considered earlier in the design process — an increasingly important advantage as AI rack densities continue to rise.


## Managing the Thermal Demands of High-Density AI


As accelerator performance and rack densities increase, removing heat efficiently becomes one of the defining challenges of AI infrastructure.


Traditional air cooling has become increasingly difficult to scale as rack power densities rise. Liquid cooling brings cooling closer to the heat source, providing a more efficient approach for managing the thermal loads generated by high-performance CPUs, GPUs, and accelerators.


Celestica integrates liquid cooling components—including Cooling Distribution Units (CDUs), direct-to-chip cold plates, thermal interface materials, and manifolds—into our high-density computing system designs. These technologies help transfer heat away from compute systems to achieve the thermal performance and reliability required for dense AI deployments.


Celestica’s capabilities span device, server, rack, and data center-level liquid cooling architectures across Celestica’s global manufacturing footprint. To support reliable performance, our advanced liquid cooling solutions feature rigorous component leak testing with traceable validation records, alongside built-in circuits for active leak notification during operation. These systems can be designed around your unique infrastructure requirements, deployment environments, and density targets.


## Extending AI Infrastructure Beyond the Traditional Data Center


The scale and speed of AI infrastructure growth are also changing how organizations view flexibility when they deploy capacity. Depending on available power, space, construction timelines, and operational requirements, that may mean expanding or retrofitting a traditional data center, deploying modular infrastructure, or using a combination of both.


Celestica’s[Modular Infrastructure](https://www.celestica.com/blog/article/solving-the-ai-power-constraint-challenge-with-modular-electrical-buildings) solutions provide an additional path to capacity by shifting more engineering, integration, and testing into a controlled factory environment. Using a modular model allows Power skids, E-Houses, and Modular Electrical Buildings (MEBs) to be deployed with fewer infrastructure requirements. Modular data center solutions can help reduce onsite complexity, deployment risk, and commissioning time while enabling infrastructure to be deployed more rapidly and predictably.


These modular solutions give hyperscalers and enterprises greater flexibility to choose their deployment model, or combination of deployment models, that best fits their capacity, infrastructure, and time-to-market requirements as AI environments scale.


## Optimizing AI Infrastructure Circularity


Deploying AI infrastructure is only part of the story. Large-scale environments must be delivered, installed, optimized, repaired, and ultimately redeployed. The operational complexity of managing thousands of systems across global locations becomes significant, particularly with the ever increasing speed of technology generations.


[Celestica Services](https://www.celestica.com/our-expertise/services/celestica-services) supports IT assets throughout their infrastructure lifecycles, from initial deployment into production environments through maintenance, support, and circular redeployment.


Once systems are operational, maintenance and technical support services help customers protect availability and extend asset life. Repair, spare-parts management, speed of deployment and third-party maintenance (TPM) capabilities help reduce disruption while supporting infrastructure across heterogeneous environments.


As equipment reaches the end of its initial deployment, circular asset recovery and redeployment services, supported by secure data sanitization and responsible e-waste recycling, help customers turn retired assets into reusable inventory and recovered value while advancing ESG goals.


## A Systems Approach to Scaling AI


The next generation of AI infrastructure will be defined not by any single component, but by how effectively the entire system works together. Compute depends on the network connecting it; increasing density reshapes power, cooling, rack design, and facility requirements; and long-term value depends on how reliably infrastructure can be deployed, maintained, and refreshed.


Celestica helps customers engineer these dependencies from the outset, bringing together expertise in design, manufacturing, integration, supply chain, and lifecycle support. This connected approach reduces complexity, accelerates time to market, and helps organizations scale infrastructure with greater confidence—from silicon to systems, rack to data center, and initial deployment through ongoing operations.
